roles.title: Story Author
roles.exchange: Present the intended message. Ask {peer} which visual choice makes that message clear.

roles.title: First-time Reader
roles.exchange: Explain one difficult reading. Ask {peer} to point to the label or visual choice that resolves it.

roles.title: Critical Editor
roles.exchange: Test one claim against the source. Ask {peer} to narrow any claim the visual cannot support.

roles.title: Evidence Checker
roles.exchange: Check a date, unit, or category used in a claim. Ask {peer} to correct any mismatch.

roles.title: Discussion Host
roles.exchange: Name a difference between two readings. Ask {peer} what the source can settle and what remains open.

81: What message does the seven-frame story communicate? Explain how changing area supports that message.
Compare the first and final frames. What does area represent? Name one step that needs a clearer explanation.
Which step supports the claim about a small voting population? State one claim the story cannot establish.
Check the dates and population groups. Why do the voting data and Senate election refer to different years?
Prepare one question that connects population size with voting influence. Explain which frame the group should check.
83: What change in middle-class jobs does the design emphasize? Explain how the order of the job groups supports it.
A line is red and slopes downward. Explain what each cue means. Which label helps you read it?
Does a falling line show fewer jobs in total? Test that claim using the vertical-axis unit.
Check the dates, unit, and gender legend. State one comparison that is valid and one that needs more data.
Prepare one question that connects gender composition with changes in job share. Keep the two variables distinct.
82: What message does the long temperature timeline communicate? Explain how its scale supports it.
Compare past observations with future scenarios. Where do the labels help you tell them apart?
Which comparison supports the story about recent warming? State a limit of the displayed evidence.
Check the time scale and the transition to projections. Which parts describe the past, and which describe possible futures?
Prepare one question about how the long scroll changes the reading of recent warming. Point to a place to compare.
84: What relationship between vaccination and outbreaks does this captured outcome communicate? Explain how repeated panels support it.
Use the legend to explain one panel. What does a dot represent, and what changes between panels?
Can this one recorded outcome show how much results vary? State what needs repeated simulation runs.
Check the vaccination-rate labels and dot colors. Distinguish a visible pattern from a guaranteed result.
Prepare one question about vaccination rate and the observed spread. Explain which panels the group should compare.
85: What does the time-lapse communicate about growth across antibiotic concentrations? Use one visible transition.
Find a pause and a later advance. Explain what the concentration labels and time display help you read.
Does the video directly show a genetic mutation? Separate visible growth from an explanation that needs other evidence.
Check the concentration boundaries and time-lapse labels. State what they allow you to compare.
Prepare one question about the link between a pause and a later advance. Choose a moment the group should replay.

81: The shrinking area emphasizes how the electorate narrows through successive filters.
The outlines help me compare population size, but I need the group labels at each transition.
The final electorate is small in the story. This does not show that every voter had equal political influence.
The voting data refer to 2010; the story concerns the 2014 Senate election.
We should compare the last electorate with the earlier population before judging the final analogy.
83: The left-to-right ordering emphasizes a shift from production jobs toward other occupations.
Red shows gender composition. A downward slope shows a smaller share of middle-class jobs.
A smaller share per 1,000 jobs does not by itself establish a decline in the absolute number of jobs.
The endpoints are 1980 and 2012, and the axis gives jobs per 1,000 middle-class jobs.
We should discuss whether the color and slope support separate parts of our interpretation.
82: The long history gives context for the rapid change near the end.
I need the labels to distinguish historical temperatures from future scenarios.
A visual comparison supports discussion of the trend, but it is not a full account of its causes.
The timeline separates past temperatures from future scenarios.
We should compare the same time interval in two parts before judging the pace of change.
84: The repeated panels suggest less spread at higher vaccination rates in this captured outcome.
The legend explains the dot states, while the panel labels identify vaccination rates.
One outcome cannot establish the variability across runs.
A visible pattern in the capture is not a guaranteed outcome of another run.
We should compare two rates, then discuss what repeated runs could add.
85: The video shows growth pausing and later advancing into stronger concentrations.
The concentration labels help me read where a growth boundary occurs.
The video shows growth; it does not directly display a mutation.
The concentration and time labels support comparisons across the plate and across moments.
We should replay a pause and advance before deciding what the evidence establishes.
